title: Plant food: how much of a forest's production is fruit and seed
licence: Numerical values cited as facts with attribution; no text, figures or datasets reproduced.

sources.citation: Ward, R. E., Zhang-Zheng, H., Abernethy, K., et al. and Kueppers, L. M. (2025). Forest Age Rivals Climate to Explain Reproductive Allocation Patterns in Forest Ecosystems Globally. Ecology Letters 28(8): e70191. doi:10.1111/ele.70191. Open-access full text read from https://www.stir.ac.uk/research/hub/file/2151418 (p.3 for the proxy, p.5 for the biome means).

items.description: Mean annual reproductive allocation of forests by biome: reproductive litterfall (flowers, fruit, seed, cone scales, husks) as a share of reproductive plus leaf litterfall, R/(R+L), which the source validates against R/NPP
items.note: p.5: 'RA exhibited a ~60% increase from boreal forests (mean = 0.082) to tropical forests (mean = 0.129), with intermediate values observed in temperate forests (mean = 0.116)'; 'standard deviations were high across all biomes (SD = 0.070, 0.084, and 0.087 for boreal, temperate, and tropical forests, respectively)'. p.3: the proxy R/(R + L) is built from litterfall and correlates with R/NPP (R2 = 0.85). R counts everything reproductive, so as the human-edible share of production it is an upper bound (D57).
